page: Microsoft Azure FX4-2ms_v2 is a memory-intensive virtual machine from the FXmsv2 family, running on the Microsoft Hyper-V hypervisor. It features an x86_64 architecture powered by an Intel Xeon 8573C processor with a high base clock speed of 4.2 GHz. The instance is configured with 1 dedicated physical core supporting 2 vCPUs via hyperthreading, alongside a massive 260 MB L3 cache. It is equipped with 84.0 GB of system memory, yielding an exceptionally high memory-to-core ratio of 42.0 GB per core. There is no local storage bundled with this instance, though it is premium storage capable, and it includes zero complimentary public IPv4 addresses.

Performance benchmarks reveal a stark contrast between single-core and multi-core capabilities. Due to the high-frequency Intel Xeon processor, single-core performance is excellent, with Geekbench single-core scores reaching the top tier and single-threaded gzip compression and bzip3 decompression showing strong results. However, because the instance only allocates 1 physical core, multi-core performance is limited, with stress-ng multi-core and Geekbench multi-core scores falling into the poor and weak categories, respectively. Memory bandwidth tests also show weaker performance for large block reads and writes, though the Passmark memory score remains average.

The FX4-2ms_v2 presents a clear architectural tradeoff, offering massive memory capacity and high single-threaded compute speed at the expense of parallel processing power and memory bandwidth. From a qualitative cost-efficiency perspective, this server is highly optimized for workloads that require a large memory footprint but do not demand high multi-threaded CPU throughput. It is well-suited for memory-intensive applications with low concurrency, such as small-scale in-memory databases, single-threaded data processing tasks, or legacy applications requiring high single-core clock speeds and substantial RAM.
